transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I've been having a really hard time coping lately after a major stressful event in my life. Ever since my divorce was finalized a couple of months ago, I've felt completely overwhelmed and just can't seem to get back on track.

Beyond feeling overwhelmed, have you been experiencing persistent symptoms like a deep loss of interest in activities you usually enjoy, significant changes in your sleep or appetite, or thoughts that life is not worth living?

No, I haven't really experienced those specific symptoms. My sleep and appetite have been mostly normal, and I definitely haven't had any thoughts of self-harm. It's more that I'm just feeling constantly stressed and struggling to adapt to my new life.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were [Adjustment Disorder, Major Depressive Disorder, Generalized Anxiety Disorder]. Based on the patient's report of a clear stressor (divorce) and the explicit denial of core depressive symptoms (loss of interest, sleep/appetite changes) and lack of pervasive anxiety symptoms beyond the adjustment to the life event, the diagnosis is most consistent with Adjustment Disorder.
